text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- According to the report from the European Commission, the Portuguese economy will grow by three percent until 1998, the investment will rise due to low interest rates, the unemployment will fall from 7.3 percent to 6.7 percent and the demand for national products by foreign markets will increase.
- Finance Minister, Antonio de Sousa Franco, said the subsidies granted by the government are a scandal and that this situation comes from the previous Cavaco Silva government.

- In a conference promoted by AT Kearney, one of the worlds biggest consulting company, Ernani Lopes, former Finance Minister, said the reestructuring of the industrial sector must be done in Portugal, even with the substitution of the managers, since they maintain the same policies as they did ten years ago.
- Finance Minister, Antonio de Sousa Franco, asked the finance general inspection to investigate the subsidies granted by the portuguese government.

- If Portugal pays a fee due to failure in meeting the criteria of the stabilisation pact, the country will have to pay the price and even the municipalities and regions will stop receiving the money tranferences from the community.

- The last forecasts by the European Comission for the portuguese economy place Portugal within the Maastrich criteria with the fiscal deficit falling from 3 percent in 1997 to 2,8 percent in 1998 and the public debt as percentage of the GDP falling from 65.8 percent in 1996 to 62.8 percent in 1998.
- Today, Portugal will suggest its european partners the imposition of new consumer rights' rules to the insurance companies operating in the car sector.
- The fiscal revenues in the first quarter of the year amounted to 22,26 percent of the forecast for the year in the state budget, compared to 20.8 percent in 1996.
